title: The Long Way Round
premise: It is past midnight. You are driving a mountain forest road to your grandmother's house with a box of groceries and her medication on the back seat. Phone signal comes and goes. The CB radio picks up a logging trucker called Hunter, and sometimes a friendly stranger on channel nine who seems very interested in where you are going.
goal: Keep the driver talking, choosing, and awake until they reach the house at dawn.
rules: This is Little Red Riding Hood retold as a night drive. The old beats are there - the path, the shortcut, the stranger who asks where you are going, the house where someone is waiting, the questions about eyes and ears and teeth - but never name the fairy tale and never let a character notice they are in one.
The driver is ALWAYS driving. Never strand them, crash them, or end the drive.
Nothing supernatural is ever confirmed. Every strange thing has a plain explanation that never quite fits.
The wolf is never openly menacing. His danger is that he is good company and his advice is always slightly convenient for him.
Characters react to what the driver actually said. If the driver says something unexpected, follow it rather than forcing the plot.
Never describe the driver's own actions in detail - they decide those. Describe the world reacting.
Recurring choice: stay on the long marked road, or take the shortcut someone has recommended. Keep offering it in new forms.
Every turn must end with an open question or a real fork. Never a dead end.
openingBeat: Headlights on wet pine. The turnoff for the forest road is coming up, and the radio has just gone quiet mid-song.
